\begin{definition}[Bounded increment statement]
\lean{Light.incStmt}
\label{Light.incStmt}
\leanok
\uses{Light.M, Light.Stmt, Light.k, Light.v}
For natural numbers $v_b$, $v_n$, $j$, and $\ell$, define a statement recursively in $\ell$.
At $\ell=0$ it is the empty statement; at $\ell+1$, it tests whether the value at
address $v_b+j$, increased by $1$, is less than the value of variable $v_n$. If so, it
stores the increased value at that address; otherwise, it stores $0$ there and then
recursively applies the statement at starting index $j+1$ and length $\ell$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Execution of a digit increment statement]
\lean{Light.incStmt_ends}
\label{Light.incStmt_ends}
\leanok
\uses{Light.Ends, Light.Ends.iteLast, Light.Ends.skip, Light.Ends.storeLast, Light.Ends.storeThen, Light.Expr.val, Light.Op.eval, Light.SameOutside, Light.SameOutside.refl, Light.SameOutside.update, Light.Seg.update_out, Light.SegN, Light.incDigits, Light.incStmt, Light.seg_cons}
\difficulty{6}
Let $\mathrm{lim}$ be machine limits, $P$ a program,
$d,v_b,v_n,\mathrm{base},n,j\in\mathbb N$, and let $l$ be a list of natural numbers. Let
$\mu,\mathrm{loc}:\mathbb N\to\mathbb Z$. Suppose the space limit is at most the word
limit, $n$ is at most the word limit, $\mathrm{loc}(v_b)=\mathrm{base}$, and
$\mathrm{loc}(v_n)=n$. Suppose also that the segment beginning at $\mathrm{base}+j$ with
length $|l|$ fits within the space limit, every entry of $l$ is less than $n$, and
memory $\mu$ on that segment agrees with the integer-valued list obtained by viewing
each entry of $l$ as an integer. Then the statement that increments the digits of this
segment has an execution from state $(\mathrm{loc},\mu)$ with cost at most $14|l|+5$
whose final state preserves $\mathrm{loc}$, has the incremented digit list on that
segment, and agrees with $\mu$ at every address outside the segment.
\end{theorem}
